text.tspan: Page 12, Technology that finally works for you
What the pen says, word for word, and what it means
FACT OR OPINION, VISIBLY
“we need a visual way to reference to the
reader facts or opinion that I do here: fact
→ backed by data; opinion → no data (yet) to
support (REF)”
Mark each claim visibly as fact (backed by data, with the
reference) or opinion (no data yet).
THE VOICE IS MINE
“[struck: and a bit,]”
Trim the quote.
FACT OR OPINION, VISIBLY
“find data to support this [beside: It is
one person's account, not a study.]”
Instead of apologising that it is one account, find the
data.
THE FIRST PAGES SELL THE BOOK
“this is what should be on that intro in
page 10”
'The biggest opportunity of your career' is the chapter's
opening.
THE MAKING-OF OUT OF THE READER'S WAY
“[struck: The 2018 book had a draft chapter
on dopamine ...]”
Cut the 2018 draft chapter.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“most readers don't know what UI or
interface is ... link?”
Explain UI and interface before using them, or link to an
explainer.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“ZX founder: what is generative AI?”
The reader asks: what is generative AI? Say it here,
briefly.
THE WEBSITE HOLDS WHAT THE PAGE CANNOT
“what about using QR codes here? → more
details”
A QR code to the site where the page needs more room.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“[struck: I recommended ... because of the
way he]”
Simplify the Kevin Kelly sentence.
THE VOICE IS MINE
“weird [circled: I have not settled.]”
'A question I have not settled' sounds odd.
MEET THE READER WHERE THEY ARE
“say it first, then link [under: Where do
you land?]”
Say what Where do you land? says, then point to it.
THE WEBSITE HOLDS WHAT THE PAGE CANNOT
“as with above we should try to find a way
to introduce the reader to these concepts
with short clear analogies, infographics,
stories & links to our site for more
details”
Every concept gets a short clear analogy, an infographic
or a story, and a link to the site for more.
